prompt_records.prompt:
Six-second top-down pixel-art RPG gameplay footage based on this supplied current studio action frame. Fixed camera centered on the target, no montage or cuts. Play action in normal fast real time without slow motion, stretched impact, slow buildup or speed ramp. Produce clear bold realistic close physical Foley, carefully synchronized to the visual event. No background music, score, singing, speech, narration, chiptune, 8-bit, cartoon or synthetic game sounds. A sharp ice projectile travels rapidly point-first and impacts the central target once, producing a forceful short air slice and a sharp realistic brittle fracture with a short ice-chip tail. The reference image uses actual animation frame 0 at 24 FPS, video time 0 equals animation 0.000s. First visible frame is 0.000s; greatest visible nonzero-alpha pixel count at animation 0.458s = video 0.458s (visual measure only, not an audio peak). Authored event timing: cast1 착탄 at animation 0.208s / video 0.208s (authored contact event); 명중 · cast1 at animation 0.208s / video 0.208s (authored contact event). The visible effect ends at animation 0.542s = video 0.542s. The full animation timeline ends at 1.500s. Times are targets for generation, not proof of model compliance. Use the pinned early action, intermediate keyframes and blank last frame as timing anchors. Do not delay the visual action until later in the clip; follow the physical-action timing in the first seconds.

Show all motion and sound in natural real time at plausible physical speed, with decisive, fast action appropriate to the event. No slow motion, speed ramp, exaggerated suspended particles or stretched impact. Maintain the explicitly requested event timing and natural sound decay; keep audio synchronized to the visible action.
